chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from one who narrated it, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
Concerning dough that was kneaded and baked, then it became known that there had been carrion in the water.
He said: “There is no problem; the fire has consumed what was in it.”

key_terms.الْمَاءَ: the water used in preparing the dough
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.مَيْتَةٌ: carrion or a dead impure creature

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on baked dough made with water that contained a dead impurity?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about dough prepared with water later found to have contained a dead impurity. The Imam عليه السلام states that there is no harm in it after baking, indicating the effect of fire in this case on what was present in the dough.
